p1.title: Passage 1
paras: For most of the history of agriculture, the farmer was also a plant breeder. At each harvest the best ears of grain, the plumpest pods and the most vigorous gourds were set aside as seed for the next season. Over centuries this patient selection produced thousands of local varieties, each adapted to a particular soil, rainfall and taste: a rice that tolerated brackish water near the coast, a millet that ripened before the monsoon failed, a bean that a certain festival required. These varieties were rarely the highest yielding, but they were dependable in the conditions that had shaped them.

The spread of commercial hybrid seed in the last century raised yields dramatically and fed growing populations, an achievement that should not be belittled. It also meant that many farmers stopped saving seed, since hybrids do not breed true, and that local varieties began to disappear from the fields. What is lost with them is not merely a curiosity of folk tradition but a store of genetic traits that breeders may one day need, when a new disease appears or the climate shifts. Seed banks preserve some of this inheritance in cold storage, but a seed kept in a vault does not go on adapting. That is why some agricultural scientists now work alongside farmers who still grow traditional varieties, treating their fields as living libraries rather than relics of a backward past.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The World Health Organization is popularly known as W.H.O. in brief. It is a specialized agency of the United Nations and was established in 1948. International health workers can be seen working in all kinds of surroundings: in deserts, jungles, mountains, coconut groves, and rice fields. They help the sick to attain health and the healthy to maintain their health. This global health team helps the local health workers in stopping the spread of what are called the communicable diseases, like cholera. These diseases can be spread from one country to another and so can be a threat to world health. W.H.O. assists different national health authorities not only in controlling diseases but also in preventing them. Total prevention is possible in a number of ways, such as vaccination and spraying of houses with substances which kill disease-carrying insects.

questions.q: The passage is primarily concerned with:
opts: The value of farmer-saved local crop varieties and the case for keeping them alive in fields.
The festivals associated with particular crops.
Methods of building cold-storage seed banks.
The superiority of hybrid seed over all traditional varieties.
questions.why: Main idea: local varieties hold traits 'breeders may one day need', and scientists now treat farmers' fields 'as living libraries'.

questions.q: According to the passage, many farmers stopped saving seed because:
opts: Seed banks supplied seed free of cost.
Local varieties were banned by law.
Traditional seeds could not be stored.
questions.why: Detail: 'many farmers stopped saving seed, since hybrids do not breed true'.

questions.q: The limitation of seed banks implied in the passage is that:
opts: They are too expensive for any country to maintain.
Their seeds lose all genetic value within a year.
Seeds stored in them do not continue to adapt to changing conditions.
questions.why: Inference: 'a seed kept in a vault does not go on adapting'.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards hybrid seed is best described as:
opts: Acknowledging its achievement while pointing out what it has cost.
questions.why: Tone: its achievement 'should not be belittled', yet it led local varieties to 'disappear from the fields'.
Vocabulary: the achievement of feeding growing populations should not be made to seem small or unimportant.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means "contagious or infectious"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: "It is a specialized agency of the United Nations." Here "specialized" means
opts: made suitable for a particular purpose
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: an agency with a specific function. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: "W.H.O. assists national health authorities not only in controlling diseases but also in preventing them." This implies that W.H.O.
opts: helps more in control than prevention
helps both in controlling and in preventing diseases
questions.why: 'Not only … but also' = both. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: In "They help the sick to attain health", "they" refers to
questions.why: Reference question: points back to the previous sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: Why are communicable diseases a threat to world health, according to the passage?
opts: They can spread from one country to another
questions.why: Detail: the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.
